subject: More images from the library summer exhibition 2025
bodyText:
photography courtesy of Ashlee Kennedy

Sent from my iPhone

mailDrop.label: Download full-resolution images
mailDrop.whatIsMissing: An iCloud Mail Drop zip named Images.zip, 4598564 bytes, holding the full-resolution versions of the Gateshead Central Library summer exhibition photographs by Ashlee Kennedy. The link lapsed on 12 July 2026 and cannot be recovered. Only the twelve reduced inline copies below survive in the message. Brian would need to resend the originals.

attachments.name: image.png
attachments.visualDescription: Colour photograph of a book signing table at the library exhibition. A bald man in a black polo shirt (Brian Rankin) holds an open deep red book while a woman in a floral blouse reaches across a white cloth table stacked with copies of the book, jars of brushes and a small red paint box. Framed paintings and interpretation panels line the wall behind.

attachments.name: image.png
attachments.visualDescription: Colour photograph, portrait orientation, of a man in a green and white striped polo shirt standing beside a bronze figure sculpture of a seated man, mounted on a printed brick-effect plinth. A camera operator in a white shirt films from the right, his monitor visible on the rig. Gallery wall map and framed works behind.

attachments.name: image.png
attachments.visualDescription: Colour photograph of exhibition visitors in conversation. An older man in a blue shirt gestures towards a bald man in a black polo shirt, with a man in a checked tweed jacket and a woman with red hair in the foreground. Framed watercolours and a display case fill the background.

attachments.name: image.png
attachments.visualDescription: Colour photograph of the sculpture unveiling. Two men lift a white cloth from a bronze seated figure on a brick-effect plinth while a woman in a pink and purple scarf smiles behind. Framed paintings hang on the pale gallery walls.

attachments.name: image.png
attachments.visualDescription: Colour photograph, portrait orientation, of an elderly couple reading a small framed exhibit and a wall panel headed The Blackett Street Story. A window with blue glazing is to the right, and two small framed works hang on the left edge.

attachments.name: image.png
attachments.visualDescription: Colour photograph of an elderly man in a striped polo shirt shaking hands with a smiling bald man in a black polo shirt who holds a certificate reading The Order of the British Empire. Behind them are exhibition boards headed Early Years and Signs of Talent.

attachments.name: image.png
attachments.visualDescription: Colour installation shot of a long gallery wall headed Friendships, Cornish and Lowry, with a life-size black and white cutout of a young Charlie Rogers at the left end. A run of framed drawings, portraits and small paintings continues along the wall with printed caption panels beneath.

attachments.name: image.png
attachments.visualDescription: Colour photograph, portrait orientation, of a seated bald man in a black polo shirt with a smiling grey-haired woman in a turquoise linen top standing behind him with her hands on his shoulders. Framed works and a black and white portrait panel are on the wall behind.

attachments.name: image.png
attachments.visualDescription: Colour photograph of the bronze sculpture of a seated man on a low brick base, with a copy of the book Charlie Rogers, Pursued by Bulldozers propped open-faced against it. The dust jacket shows a colourful terraced street scene in red, blue and ochre. Gold-framed paintings hang on the wall behind.

attachments.name: image.png
attachments.visualDescription: Colour photograph of a bald man in a black polo shirt speaking to camera in front of an exhibition board headed Gateshead Art Society, which carries a black and white photograph of Charlie Rogers. A television camera on a tripod is at the right edge, and a framed winter park painting hangs behind.

attachments.name: image.png
attachments.visualDescription: Colour photograph, portrait orientation, of the signing table with visitors. A bald man in a black polo shirt sits at the left with stacked books, a jar of brushes and a red paint box; three visitors including a woman in a bright purple floral dress look on. Exhibition panels headed London and Royal Academy behind.

attachments.name: Image-1.jpg
attachments.visualDescription: Colour photograph, tall portrait crop, of a blonde woman in a navy striped top with gold stars looking at a gold-framed Charlie Rogers painting of a steep cobbled back lane between terraced houses, worked in soft washes of grey, pink and blue. To the right is the Gateshead Art Society panel with a black and white portrait of Charlie.

The bronze seated figure sits on its brick plinth between them.

attachments.name: image.png
attachments.visualDescription: Colour photograph of the reporter in a white shirt holding a microphone towards a bald man in a black polo shirt, in front of a wall panel headed The Long Road to Paris with a route map. A framed painting of a park in winter hangs to the left.

attachments.name: image.png
attachments.visualDescription: Colour photograph of the bald man in a black polo shirt talking with the reporter beneath a panel reading Keeping my Mittens on. A silver-framed Charlie Rogers watercolour of a bare winter park and a small framed pencil sketch titled Two girls, 1978 hang alongside.

attachments.name: image.png
attachments.visualDescription: Colour photograph taken past the bronze seated figure in the right foreground, looking through to the bald man in black gesturing and the reporter holding a microphone, standing beneath the Keeping my Mittens on panel and a route map.

attachments.name: image.png
attachments.visualDescription: Colour photograph of the interview in progress, camera and boom microphone in the centre of frame, the bald man in a black polo shirt on the left and the reporter on the right. A framed winter park painting with a caption card reading Shipley Art Gallery, December is behind them.

attachments.name: image.png
attachments.visualDescription: Colour photograph of the bald man in black and the reporter standing either side of the bronze seated figure on its brick plinth, both smiling, with the Keeping my Mittens on panel and a framed woodland watercolour behind.

attachments.name: image.png
attachments.visualDescription: Colour photograph, portrait orientation, of a man in a green and white striped polo shirt standing beside the bronze seated figure, looking at camera with a wry expression. The route map panel is behind.

attachments.name: Image-1.jpg
attachments.visualDescription: Colour photograph of the bald man in a black polo shirt in close-up, filmed by the broadcast camera at the right edge. Behind him hangs a silver-framed Charlie Rogers watercolour of a park in winter, bare trees, a monument and small figures, worked in pale washes with a signature visible along the lower edge. A caption card reads Shipley Art Gallery, December.

attachments.visualDescription: A photograph of an archive black and white print, not a painting. subject: Charlie and Bruce
bodyText:
Hi Tom
Maybe this one where it would seem he is looking down at the dog.

Sent from my iPhone

attachments.name: IMG_6360.jpeg
attachments.visualDescription: A photograph of an archive black and white print, not a painting. Charlie Rogers stands in his studio in a light jacket over a dark jumper and gingham shirt, head tilted down, lifting brushes and quills from a small pot. Behind him hang four of his framed works, including a pit ponies or horse scene, a Gateshead corner shop street scene and a steep terraced back lane with a lamp post; a longcase clock stands at the right. Brian suggests the downward gaze reads as looking at the dog.

subject: Pursued by Bulldozers
bodyText:
Hi Tom

I can’t remember if we have included the book on the website. Here is some info.

Cheers
Brian

Pursued by Bulldozers

SPECIAL EDITION - EXCLUSIVE TO THIS WEBSITE

To celebrate the launch of the new website, a limited edition of just 100 copies is being made available.

Each copy will be embossed with the bespoke Charlie Rogers logo and signed personally by author Brian Rankin.

It is anticipated that the monetary value of each copy will increase over time, although this is not guaranteed.

PRICE £25

Pursued by Bulldozers is the story of a self-taught artist for whom the streets, back lanes and everyday scenes of life in Gateshead and Newcastle were the inspiration for a little-known collection of sketches and paintings that are receiving widespread local and regional acclaim, both from the public and the artistic community. As the name implies, Charlie’s work captured edifices, landmarks, images and personalities just before they were lost forever to modernisation in the rapidly changing urban communities of the late 20th century North East.

Sent from my iPhone

product.title: Greeting Card Collection
product.description: It would be nice to include this collection on the website.
product.notes: Attached PDF is titled Charlie Rogers Christmas Card Selection and contains five card designs, each captioned Charlie Rogers The Collection and carrying the line All Charlie Rogers paintings and sketches © Charles Rogers Junior. The five cards, verbatim from the PDF, are: The Monument with Snow, Newcastle-on-Tyne 1996, Watercolour; St Cuthbert’s Church, Gateshead-on-Tyne 1982, Oil; Bensham Road, Gateshead 1970, Watercolour; Street meeting with snow, Gateshead 1972, Watercolour; Cotfield Street, Bensham, Gateshead-on-Tyne ????, Watercolour. The date for Cotfield Street is given in the source as ???? and is therefore unknown. Pack composition, card dimensions and whether envelopes are included are not stated. This message was still unread in Tom's mailbox when catalogued.

attachments.name: Charlie Rogers Christmas Card Selection.pdf
attachments.visualDescription: Not a single image. A five-page PDF presenting the Charlie Rogers Christmas card selection, one card design per page, each headed Charlie Rogers The Collection with the painting title, place, year and medium beneath and a copyright line for Charles Rogers Junior. The five reproduced works are The Monument with Snow, Newcastle-on-Tyne 1996 (watercolour), St Cuthbert’s Church, Gateshead-on-Tyne 1982 (oil), Bensham Road, Gateshead 1970 (watercolour), Street meeting with snow, Gateshead 1972 (watercolour) and Cotfield Street, Bensham, Gateshead-on-Tyne, undated (watercolour). The page images themselves did not render on read, only the caption text, so the artwork colouring has not been seen.
